title: 1675 Mercock Land Dispute
summary: A 1675 record preserves Tackapousha challenging colonial possession of "Mercock" land, stating that the land Hempstead enjoyed had not been paid for. The statement places Merrick/Mercock land within ongoing disputes over payment, authority, and colonial occupation. Tackapousha's challenge shows Native diplomacy and legal resistance rather than land loss as inevitable or uncontested.
address_label: Merrick / Hempstead south shore land dispute landscape
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land through the Mercock/Merrick land reference and south shore Hempstead context.
why_this_matters: The 1675 Mercock dispute shows that Native leaders challenged colonial land claims and named unpaid land as an injustice. Dispossession appears here as a contested process involving diplomacy, law, pressure, and resistance.
